cells.tense: You're seeing clearly while you're still in the middle of the work.
cells.ask: Show one piece of the work to someone who wouldn't usually see it. Let their plain question tell you what's actually sharp. You don't need defending, only another set of eyes on it.
cells.core:
You've kept a beginner's eye inside the thing you do often. Most people lose that after the first year — the work hardens and the fresh look goes. You still catch it new and sharpen it where people can see, and that pairing is less common than it sounds.

The practice isn't the only thing you're doing anymore. You're also watching yourself do it. That's the deeper feed here, not more hours on the work — more sitting with the patterns underneath it. One image from a sitting comes to mind before it's about anything else. When are you making room for that, as opposed to the next round of doing?
cells.sheetLine: A beginner's eye kept sharp by steady practice — that's you both.

cells.tense: You're rehearsing a moment of clarity that hasn't arrived yet, and calling the rehearsal discipline.
cells.ask: When you sit down to the practice this week, want one thing: any wanting wants. You keep up the motion but stop steering toward the verdict. Let it be a practice, unfinished and unfinished-light.
cells.core:
Sitting down with nothing to prove and nothing to catch — the sitting is its own event and the hours pass unmarked. Not a posture you need to hold. Just the thing you keep walking past.

Instead you're watching for the arrival of a clear sight as if it were a scheduled event. Every practice gets read for signs it's come, every quiet stretch gets audited for progress. The watch is exact and tireless, and it has quietly taken over the room. The moment you're waiting for doesn't survive being watched. You can see it happen in a muscle: it wants to be fresh, enters a frame you've already built for it, and ends up another rehearsal. What would be here if you sat down with nothing in mind about what it should produce?
cells.sheetLine: You're watching for clarity so hard it can't arrive.

cells.tense: You stopped coming to your own practice as someone with a say in what happens there.
cells.ask: Wash a single dish to the standard you'd want a guest to find it. Choose that standard, hold it to the end, and let it be enough. That's the whole ask — one thing, chosen, finished.
cells.core:
The clear look that used to start everything has gone quiet and it didn't leave a note. The practice still happens, and the motions come out on time. There's no weight in it and no argument either.

What's absent is probably availability, not insight. You know how to refine when someone hands the refinement to you. Starting something in a room with no one watching and choosing the standard yourself is another muscle entirely, and it hasn't been in the room for a while. It's steady and low, not bright. The way back is to pick one small thing with an edge to it and carry it through to done, however unremarkable it looks.

cells.tense: You're seeing clearly in the middle of the practice and treating the clarity as the practice's, not yours.
cells.ask: When something comes clear in your next session, say it in a full sentence, either out loud or in writing. Plain words. The sentence is yours to keep; the session is just where it showed up.
cells.core:
The first clean cut of sight has been coming for a while, and you've been calling it the practice working well. You credit the discipline, the method, the fact of showing up — everything except the one doing it. It's real and you're already standing in it, but the claim hasn't made it back to you.

That's a quiet cost. What arrives gets filed as result instead of recognized as yours, and recognition is what would let it feed the next round instead of settling as outcome. There's a moment when you could tell yourself the truth about who is looking. What happens in that moment decides whether it keeps growing or keeps getting signed by the method.
cells.sheetLine: What you see is yours. You keep filing it under practice.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person has somatically forgotten their own standards in the practice — the record only says availability is absent, not that the body has lost the precedent. The reader could object that their body remembers plenty and still goes tight. The ask survives being wrong: washing one dish to the standard you'd want a guest to find it is still useful whether or not availability is the missing piece. The sentence that serves me is 'You know you're not fully in the practice' — it presumes a self-audit I cannot see, and it goes.
